title: Choose the right format, ready your phone, protect privacy
course_title: Voice Notes, Photos & Videos for Expression

say: Choose the right format, get your phone ready, and protect privacy.
This is the video for module one of Voice Notes, Photos and Videos for Expression.
Your phone gives you four ways to send a message: typed text, a voice note, a photo and a video.

say: No format is best for everything. A woman who always types may send three long paragraphs about a leaking pipe, when one photo would do.

say: You do not need an expensive phone. You need to know where things are, and how much data each kind of media takes.

say: And before any recording skill come habits that protect you and the people you record.

say: Typed text carries exact details: numbers, names and times, easy to copy later. A photo shows what something looks like, but does not explain.

panel.heading: What each format carries well
left: Text: easy to search and copy
Photo: damage, a product, a place
Photo: shows but does not explain

say: A voice note carries tone and warmth, but numbers are hard to copy from it. A video shows movement, steps and a route, and it is the heaviest on data.

panel.heading: What each format carries well

Photo: damage, a product, a place
Photo: shows but does not explain

say: First: must the listener copy or keep an exact detail, like a number, an address or an amount? Then that detail goes in text, even if the rest is a voice note.

panel.heading: Four questions choose the format
items: Exact detail to copy or keep? Type it.
Does it depend on how it looks? Add a photo.
Movement, order or sound? A short video.
Feeling or tone? A voice note, or a call.

say: Second: does the message depend on what something looks like? Then add a photo.

Feeling or tone? A voice note, or a call.

say: Third: does it depend on movement, order or sound, like the route from the junction? Then a short video.

say: Fourth: does it depend on feeling or tone, like thanks, an apology or a delicate request? Then a voice note, or a call.

say: There is a fifth option: do not record at all. A recording can be forwarded and taken out of context. For a quarrel or bad news, call or visit.

panel.heading: Four questions choose the format
items: Exact detail to copy or keep? Type it.
Does it depend on how it looks? Add a photo.
Movement, order or sound? A short video.
Feeling or tone? A voice note, or a call.
panel.rule: Serious or emotional? Call or visit instead of recording.

say: For example, Halima in Kaduna has water dripping from her bathroom ceiling after rain. Her landlord is an elderly man who prefers calls and voice notes.
She types the exact details: Flat 3B, leak started Tuesday 14th after the rain.

cards.d: Flat 3B, leak started Tuesday 14th after the rain. Exact details the landlord can copy.
One wide shot of the ceiling stain, one close-up of the drip with a bucket underneath.
A greeting, the problem in one sentence, and a polite request for a plumber this week.

say: She takes two photos: one wide shot of the whole ceiling, and one close-up of the drip. A video would add little, so she skips it to save data.

cards.d: Flat 3B, leak started Tuesday 14th after the rain. Exact details the landlord can copy.
One wide shot of the ceiling stain, one close-up of the drip with a bucket underneath.
A greeting, the problem in one sentence, and a polite request for a plumber this week.

say: He likes to be greeted properly, so she records a 25-second voice note. She sends it first, then the photos, then the typed line he can forward to the plumber.

say: A one-minute voice note is usually well under 1 MB. A camera photo is often 2 to 6 MB. One minute of full HD video is often 50 MB or more.

say: Consent means the person agrees freely, knowing where the recording will go. For children, ask the parent or guardian.
Then run six checks. Did they agree? Do they know where it goes? Background checked for house numbers or school badges? No cards or PINs? Location tag off? Fine if forwarded?

panel.heading: Before you press record or send
items: Did they agree?
Do they know where it goes?
Background checked?
No numbers, cards or PINs?
Location tag off?
Fine if forwarded?

say: Some things must never be photographed or recorded: your ATM card number or the three digits on its back, and your BVN or NIN.

panel.heading: Never record or photograph these
items: ATM card number or the three digits on its back
Your BVN or NIN
PINs, OTPs and passwords
Full bank statements

say: Also PINs, one-time passwords, which we call OTPs, other passwords, and full bank statements.

panel.heading: Never record or photograph these
items: ATM card number or the three digits on its back
Your BVN or NIN
PINs, OTPs and passwords
Full bank statements

say: No genuine bank, network or government office will ask you to send these as a photo, voice note or video. If someone asks, treat it as a scam.

items: ATM card number or the three digits on its back

PINs, OTPs and passwords
Full bank statements
panel.rule: If anyone asks you to send these, treat it as a scam.

say: To remember. Text for exact details, photo for looks, video for steps, and a voice note for tone, with the key number typed underneath.
Turn off video auto-download on mobile data. Ask before you record anyone, and check every background before you send.

panel.heading: Remember
